name: Palestine

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 93%, Christian about 1 to 2%
facts.currency: Egyptian pound, Israeli new shekel, Jordanian dinar

system_note: The Palestinian Authority governs parts of the West Bank; Hamas still runs Gaza.
snapshot: A year after the Gaza ceasefire, Hamas still governs the strip, and Abbas postponed the first Palestinian parliamentary election in nearly 20 years to 2027.
culture: Palestinian identity is bound up with the land and with the memory of the 1948 Nakba, when some 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled. Embroidered thobes, the keffiyeh and olive harvests are national symbols. Dabke dance and the poetry of Mahmoud Darwish are loved across the Arab world. Bethlehem and Jerusalem's Old City hold sites sacred to Christians and Muslims.
society: Palestinians have a young, highly educated population but live under Israeli occupation in the West Bank, where settlements and settler violence have expanded, and in a Gaza largely destroyed by war, where most people are displaced and dependent on aid. Millions of refugees and their descendants live in Jordan, Lebanon and Syria. Most countries now recognise Palestine as a state.

story: Palestinians last voted for a parliament in 2006. Hamas won, Fatah refused to accept it, and after brief civil war Hamas took Gaza in 2007, leaving Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority in charge of parts of the West Bank. Abbas was elected in 2005 to a five-year term. He is now 90 and still president. A whole generation of Palestinians has never voted. In 2026, they came close, then didn't.

Under pressure from Western and Arab governments to reform the Palestinian Authority so it could play a role in post-war Gaza, Abbas decreed in July that legislative elections would be held on 28 November, the first in nearly 20 years, with a presidential vote in early 2027 (Doha Institute). A new law required every candidate to recognise the PLO as the sole representative of the Palestinian people, effectively excluding Hamas unless it changed its stance. Separately, he scheduled the first direct elections for the Palestinian National Council, the PLO's parliament, whose members have always been appointed. Then, on 9 October, Abbas postponed the legislative vote to 11 September 2027, to be held together with the presidential election, saying conditions were not right and noting that Israel had not let election materials or observers into Gaza (Al Jazeera). Gaza itself, a year after the US-brokered ceasefire, remains in limbo: Hamas still governs it, while the technocrats meant to run it under Trump's Board of Peace wait in Cairo for permission to enter (AP via ClickOrlando).
briefing.power: The Palestinian Authority, created by the 1990s Oslo Accords, governs parts of the West Bank under Israeli occupation; its parliament has not functioned since 2007, and Abbas rules by decree. Gaza is run by Hamas. The PLO represents Palestinians internationally. Palestine is a UN observer state recognised by most of the world.
briefing.holders: President Mahmoud Abbas (Fatah), since 2005; in Gaza, Hamas.
